title: Tool-call JSON guardrails and actionable messages
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Provide a concise, machine- and human-friendly JSON schema format for tool/function calls, enforce parameter validation at runtime, and map validation failures to actionable error messages (developer-facing + user-facing). This ticket captures the spec, runtime behaviors, telemetry surface, and message catalog so SDKs and Console can present consistent remediation steps.
background: Current function call validation is tolerant but opaque: runtime rejects or returns generic failures. Customers and platform teams need predictable, debuggable validation errors and guidance for quick fixes. This work spans schema authoring conventions, server-side validation modes (strict/soft/repair), error code taxonomy, and SDK-friendly hints for client-side validation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Define a compact JSON schema extension for tool params (annotations for required, coercion modes, example values, and 'repair_suggestion').
2) Implement server runtime validator with three modes: strict (reject), permissive (coerce if safe), and diagnostic (accept but attach warnings).
3) Error catalog published with stable 3-part codes (category.code.subcode) and human-readable remediation.
4) SDKs surfaced errors with 'fix_suggestion' and pointer to failing field.
5) Unit and integration tests covering edge cases and streaming scenarios.
decisions:
- Use a small annotation set instead of full JSON Schema to limit surface area.
- Validation mode configurable per-route via API config; default is 'diagnostic' for backward compatibility.
- Error codes follow pattern: VLD.<FIELD>.<REASON> (e.g., VLD.body.MISSING_REQUIRED).
- Repair suggestions prioritized: type-coercion -> default fill -> user-visible instruction.
tradeoffs:
- Small annotation set reduces expressiveness vs full JSON Schema but simplifies runtime and error messaging.
- 'Permissive' mode reduces user-visible failures at the cost of silent behavioral changes; will require telemetry and opt-in.
- Inline repair suggestions can leak implementation details; messages must be curated to avoid security exposure.
implementation_plan:
1) Spec: author 'call_param_manifest' doc and examples (this ticket).
2) Runtime: plumb validation mode into request pipeline, implement validator module with clear error envelope. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342.
3) SDKs: map error envelope to typed exceptions and convenience validators. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412.
4) Console: display pointer to failing parameter, suggestion, and link to schema.
5) QA: fuzz schema and partial-streaming call cases.
6) Rollout: stage on staging with diagnostic mode, enable strict on a small set of test routes, monitor regressions for 3 days.
work_log: 2026-03-10: Ticket created by Ava. Drafted initial annotation set and rationale.
2026-03-11: Spike implemented validator prototype (local). Found edge-case with nested optional objects and streaming partial payloads.
2026-03-12: Design review with PM/UX: agreed to include 'repair_suggestion' string in schema; UX will display succinct hint and 'show details' to avoid noise.
2026-03-13: Rafael pushed runtime prototype and opened PR 8342. Added telemetry hooks for error codes and repair actions.
2026-03-13: Added unit tests for numeric coercion, missing required fields, and enum mismatches.
reviewer_feedback: PM (Jared Morales) 2026-03-12: Favor conservative defaults. Make permissive mode opt-in per-route.
Security (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12: Ensure repair suggestions do not leak sensitive param values; sanitize examples.
Design (Lina Park) 2026-03-12: Console should collapse long messages and link to schema examples.
Runtime (Diego Alvarez) 2026-03-13: Suggest attaching failing token offsets for streaming calls to improve debugging latency issues.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for validator: missing required, wrong type, out-of-range, enum mismatch, extra unknown fields.
- Integration: run against sample models and ensure streaming partial payloads are validated incrementally.
- Backward-compat: run preexisting customer routes in 'diagnostic' mode for 72 hours and compare error rates.
- Fuzzing: random param shapes to ensure validator remains robust and does not OOM.
telemetry_requirements:
- Emit VLD.* error codes with route, model_name, validation_mode, and user_organization (anonymized).
- Track 'repair_applied' boolean and 'repair_type' (coercion|default|trim).
- Record time-to-first-failure for streaming calls to detect position of invalid data.
- Dashboard: validation failure rate by route, top failing fields, and remediation frequency.
rollback_plan:
- If regressions observed after enabling 'strict' on canary routes, revert config to 'diagnostic' and ship hotfix that relaxes specific failing constraints.
- Hotfix approach: add per-route exception list for allowed legacy shapes while we notify customers.
